title: Rabbi David Tawil: Rosh Hashanah - "My Father, My King"

chapters.title: Contradictions of Rosh Hashanah
chapters.about: seriousness vs festivity, comparison with Yom Kippur

chapters.title: Ezra HaSofer and Fasting on Rosh Hashanah
chapters.about: historical exiles, Ezra HaSofer, prohibition against fasting

chapters.title: Avinu Malkeinu: Father and King
chapters.about: dual relationship with Hashem, awe of King vs love of Father

chapters.title: Crowning the King and Shofar Blowing
chapters.about: Malkeinu, Malchuyot, shofar as royal arrival, establishing relationship

chapters.title: Avinu, Har Sinai, and Mercy
chapters.about: judge as Father, Akeidat Yitzchak, covenant, throne of rachamim

chapters.about: Musaf prayer, children vs servants in judgment

chapters.title: Rachum versus Chanun
chapters.about: mercy vs graciousness, speeding ticket parable

chapters.about: God as judge and witness, self-improvement, table conduct

chapters.title: Q&A: Shofar and Second Night Preparations

summary: Rabbi Tawil addresses the apparent contradiction on Rosh Hashanah between somber fear of Hashem as King and festive celebration of Hashem as Father. He explores the central theme of Avinu Malkeinu, the symbolism of the shofar, the Musaf prayer Hayom Harat Olam, and the difference between rachum and chanun. He concludes by answering questions regarding proper focus during shofar blowing and halakhot for preparing food for the second night of the holiday.

questions: How does Rosh Hashanah balance fear of judgment with festive celebration?
What is the dual theme of Avinu Malkeinu in Rosh Hashanah prayers?
Why are confessions of sin absent from the Rosh Hashanah service?
What is the difference between rachum and chanun?
What should a person do during the blowing of the shofar?
When may preparations begin for the second night of Rosh Hashanah?
